The Gibka-S self-propelled very short-range air defense system, based on a modified Tigr 4×4 armored vehicle, was seen conducting live-fire exercises, with drones serving as the primary targets.
The system uses roof-mounted launchers capable of firing Igla-S or 9K333 Verba MANPADS, using the 9M336, 9M342, or 9M39 surface-to-air missiles. The vehicle can carry four additional missiles internally. Its launcher has 360° traverse and an elevation range of −5° to +80°.
It is still too early to classify the Gibka-S specifically as a counter-drone system. However, its high mobility and ability to rapidly relocate could potentially improve the survivability and responsiveness of very short-range air defenses, including against small UAVs.

The U.S. Missile Defense Agency has awarded Raytheon a $745 million contract to manufacture, supply, and maintain Standard Missile-3 Block IIA (SM-3 IIA) interceptors for the U.S. Navy (USN).
Under the contract, production will take place at Raytheon facilities in Tucson, Arizona, and Huntsville, Alabama.
The contract is separate from previous agreements covering increased production, procurement, and maintenance of SM-3 interceptors, with the latest deal covering entirely new orders.
